problem: Prior spatial-concept approaches only picked the single likeliest goal position from a speech instruction and then ran a planner. This can select a far or unreachable goal (e.g., inside an obstacle) and gives no principled treatment of the whole trajectory.
motivation: Home robots should follow spoken place instructions such as 'Go to the kitchen' using place names learned from the user, with no hand-specified goal coordinates and no per-goal RL policy training. Casting planning as control-as-inference on the same Bayesian generative model (SpCoSLAM) lets the instruction act as an implicit reward, so the trajectory is optimized jointly with the place semantics.
key_idea: Path planning is formulated as maximizing the trajectory posterior p(tau | speech, x0, learned SpCoSLAM parameters) with a Viterbi search over grid cells. The speech-conditioned emission log-likelihood serves as the reward, following control-as-inference.
insight: Optimizing the whole trajectory against the emission probability handles many-to-many place-word relations without explicit goals. Ambiguous names resolve to the nearest instance, and usage frequency, multiple names, and AND/OR compositions all emerge from the likelihood (Fig. 5 qualitative examples). In the simulator comparison (Table 1), Viterbi SpCoNavi raised Near-NSR to 0.75 against 0.35 for the goal-point baseline, which shows the gain comes from joint trajectory inference rather than the A* planner. The A* approximation is about 147x faster but loses optimality (NSR 0.85).
method: Problem formulation: find u_{1:T} maximizing p(tau | y_{1:T}, x0, Theta_G), where the same speech observation is assumed at every step up to horizon T.

Marginalization: marginalize over spatial concept C, position-distribution index i, and word sequence S. Speech is represented by an N-best bag-of-words, giving a product of multinomials and Gaussians per cell.
Cost-map motion model: p(x_t|m) from the occupancy grid cost map (0 at obstacles, lower near them) is multiplied into the motion model to keep paths safe.
Viterbi inference: compute the probability for every grid cell and plan the path with dynamic programming (Viterbi) on a 5-action grid (stay/up/down/left/right).

CaI link: the emission probability p(y|x,Theta_G)=exp(r), so the reward is the log-likelihood. Speech generalizes the binary optimality variable, needs no manual reward design, and replaces RL policy search with the learned generative model.

A* approximation: sample J candidate goals from position distributions, run A* with cost = -log emission probability, and choose the minimum cumulative-cost path. This is greedy and sub-optimal but much faster.
Learned prerequisites: the map, spatial concepts and language model come from SpCoSLAM or Gibbs sampling and are fixed at navigation time.

setting.backbone: SpCoSLAM Bayesian generative model (learned spatial concepts) with Viterbi/A* planning; Julius DNN-HMM speech recognition
setting.training_data: Unsupervised spatial-concept learning in each environment: about 15 training utterances/positions per place, 9-10 concepts per environment; real-world experiment uses SpCoSLAM 2.0 parameters learned on the albert-b-laser-vision dataset
setting.observation: Occupancy grid map, laser range, speech utterance (N-best ASR); no vision features used
setting.action_space: discrete grid moves: stay, up, down, left, right (plus diagonals in the real-data experiment)
setting.simulator: SIGVerse 3.0 (Unity + ROS), HSR robot, 10 Sweet Home 3D three-bedroom homes
setting.privileged: Pre-learned map, spatial concepts and lexicon; word dictionary given in advance; latent indices C_t and i_t assumed almost accurately estimated; start position known

numbers.extra: planning horizon T=200; computation time 39.56x10^2 s
J=10 goal candidates; 26.86 s compute (147.25x faster)

numbers_note: Real-robot experiment reports only NSR average 0.667 over nine taught places (same as baseline C), on a logged dataset with no table; other results are qualitative figures. Baselines in Table 1: (C) 0.90/0.35/84.11, (D) 0.95/0.30/88.26, (E) 0.35/0.10/106.14 (NSR/Near-NSR/PL).
results: On the 20-trial 'bedroom' task in SIGVerse, Viterbi SpCoNavi reached NSR 1.00 and Near-NSR 0.75 with PL 63.15, beating the spatial-concept goal-point baseline (0.90 / 0.35 / 84.11) and the database baseline (NSR 0.95). The A* approximation was 147x faster with NSR 0.85 and the shortest PL (48.88). On the logged real-environment data, average NSR was 0.667, equal to baseline C.
limitations: Global planning on a static grid map. The Viterbi search is very slow (~3956 s per plan), and the fast A* variant is only sub-optimal, sometimes stopping short of the target.

Gaussian position distributions can extend across walls, causing failures (real-environment error case). Instruction parsing is limited to bag-of-words with a trigger phrase, and out-of-vocabulary or unknown places are not handled.

Evaluation is small: one word ('bedroom'), 20 trials, simulator homes. The real-world part is qualitative and uses logged dataset parameters rather than an online robot; the sim setting assumes accurately estimated latent variables.
